land.text: the fifteen islands of the Southern and Northern Cook Islands

predecessors.note: 'In 1901 the islands were included within the boundaries of the Colony of New Zealand by Order in Council', effective 11 June 1901, after a British protectorate from 1888. The new-zealand dossier (oc-02-a) draws the Cook Islands within New Zealand from 1907 and as a client from 1965.

capitals.name: Avarua
capitals.note: 'The capital is Avarua, located on the island of Rarotonga'; infobox '21°12′S 159°46′W'.

correction.text: the fifteen islands, 'divided into two distinct groups: the Southern Cook Islands and the Northern Cook Islands of coral atolls'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row): the country Cook Is. is cells: 1 (about 253 km2) (the Rarotonga cell only; the northern atolls are not drawn) against the page's 236.7 km2.

ledger.note: 1965: the Cook Islands become self-governing: infobox 'Self-governance: 4 August 1965'; 'On 4 August 1965, a constitution was promulgated'; the status is 'self-governing while in free association with New Zealand'.

certainty.note: Island coasts. The page records a maritime boundary treaty with the United States (11 June 1980), no land border.

sources.title: Cook Islands
sources.note: British protectorate 1888, boundary of New Zealand 11 June 1901, self-governance 4 August 1965 in free association, area 236.7 km2, fifteen islands, Avarua with coordinates, 1980 US maritime treaty.

notes: Written by oc-02-x. One page opened (Cook Islands). The page does not mention the Cook Islands Constitution Act 1964. 'On 11 June 1980, the United States signed a treaty with the Cook Islands specifying the maritime border', 'relinquishing any American claims to Penrhyn, Pukapuka, Manihiki, and Rakahanga'; those islands are already inside the state's shape, so no gain event is entered. The page gives 15 islands and a land area of about 236.7 km2; the gazetteer shape is one cell at Rarotonga only. The page does not mention Tokelau. The new-zealand dossier (oc-02-a) records the Cook Islands as a client (vassal_start 1965, counterpart cook-islands); this dossier is the state it names, so the renderer must not draw the same land twice.
